26y8u2eiy39: Before April 2022, these versions required the **Microsoft Monitoring Agent (MMA)**. The **modern unified solution** removes this dependency and broadens the features. On 2012 R2, it installs the Defender antivirus and the EDR sensor; on 2016, the antivirus is built in and it installs the sensor; on 2019 and later, everything is built in. Prerequisites: up-to-date system and antivirus platform, a recent package downloaded from the portal before each new installation, and update of the sensor component through Windows Update (or WSUS / Configuration Manager). Limit to remember: the local interface of these versions is limited; avoid any feature that waits for a user decision on a server, and note that **not all ASR rules apply to all systems**. Another rule: a system upgrade on 2016 or earlier requires you to **offboard and uninstall** Defender beforehand, then reinstall.
3weoq8xry5: The migration removes the MMA workspace, removes a SCEP client if needed, enables and updates the antivirus on 2016, installs the unified solution and applies the onboarding script. If a **third-party antivirus** is in place, the recommended sequence first installs the solution in **passive mode**, onboards, applies the updates, then removes the other product and the passive configuration. Configuration Manager 2207 and later can automate the deployment; before that, the procedure is manual.
